name: Make
author: unattributed

provenance.from: Aminet dev/amos/IntuiExtend20b.lha, distribution/bonus/makelib/AMOSPro_Make.lib. The same table also ships in IntuiExtend16.lha.
provenance.note: Not part of IntuiExtend: it rides along in that archive's `bonus` drawer, which also carries builds of EasyLife and Misc by other authors again. Andrew Burton's AMOS Extensions List records it independently at slot 17 as 'Make Lib' version 1.3, and points at these same two archives as where to find it -- so the list and the artefact agree, and this is the list being followed to its stated source rather than a discovery. The binary's $VER says 1.30 where the list says 1.3; same release, and the cookie is kept. No author is named in the doc or the binary.
provenance.redistribution: Carried in an Aminet upload as a bonus item. No licence text ships with it and its author is unrecorded, so terms are unstated.

findings: Explains eight of the corpus's programs at slot 17, which is what turned it up: extscan could not account for that slot until this library was read. An anonymous author's answer to a complaint in his own first line -- "my opinion is that AMOSPro is missing usable memory allocation routines and it doesn't have any routines to handle lists and nodes at all" -- so it is exec's AllocMem, AllocVec and a malloc with its own free-all, eight of exec's list routines, a C-shaped stdio over dos.library, and three graphics keywords that belong to neither. Read from the 2,344-byte hunk (38 jump-table entries, 32 of them keywords) against Make_lib.doc, which documents every one; the slot is confirmed from both sides, `move.l a3,$1f8(a5)` in routine 0 and "The extension number of MakeLib is 17." in the doc. Four places where the binary and the manual disagree, all recorded in the NOTES: Ma Fopen's third mode is not "a" but every character that is not R or W; Ma Fread, Ma Fwrite and Ma Fseek all return their own last argument when the handle is zero, because the null arm branches past the instruction that would have written the result; Ma Point is not AMOS's Point, ignoring the clip window and walking EcCurrent where AMOS walks EcLogic; and Ma Realloc(0,n) branches to the exit without writing a return value at all. One further defect is the binary's own: Ma Paste Icon takes the plane count from the SCREEN and never reads the icon's, so an icon with fewer planes has its missing ones filled from the next record in the bank. Two jump-table entries past the last keyword are dead -- routine 36 is the error text "Out of memory!" and routine 37 the identity banner, and nothing in the library calls either, because every failure here is reported by returning 0. Made MemPool in src/amiga/exec.ts shared: it was written inside sln.ts with a note saying it would move if a second extension ever wanted AllocMem, and this is that extension.
notes: AmigaOS memory and list handling for AMOS: AllocMem, exec lists, vectors and a malloc.
